title: How Anti-Corruption Threatens Investment

How Anti-Corruption Threatens Investment

Christopher Beddor

Gavekal Dragonomics | 7 Aug 2026

China’s anti-corruption campaign continues to tear through government and military ranks at an astonishing pace. So far in 2026, the campaign has taken down the highest-ranking military official, and reportedly may have toppled the chief banking regulator. The most recent high-profile target is Ma Xingrui, who previously headed provincial governments in Xinjiang and Guangdong, and is now the third sitting Politburo member to be removed in the past year.Ma’s case reportedly involved a web of real-estate and construction deals dating back about a decade. In that respect, his case is not unique: the official misconduct alleged by anti-corruption investigators is often related to projects, especially land and construction deals. The stepped-up anti-corruption campaign suggests that investigators are focusing far more on irregularities in government project contracts than in the past—a heightened level of scrutiny that may be one of the factors dragging down infrastructure and other investment.
